senses.gloss: रुक्म- + पुर रुक्म- + पुर, n. the name of a fabulous town, Pañc. 84, 7.

रुक्म रुक्म, i. e. रुच् + म,
 I. adj. Clear, bright.
 II. n. (ved. m., Chr. 293, 2 = Rigv. i. 88, 2).
 1. Gold.
 2. Iron.
 III. m. A golden chain, Chr. 290, 4 = Rigv. i. 64, 4.

रुक्मिन् रुक्मिन्, i. e. रुक्म + इन्,
 I. m. The name of a prince, slain by बलराम.
 II. f. मिणी, A princess [] carried off and married by Kṛṣṇa, Mālav. d. 77; cf. Wilson, Hind. Theatr. 2. ed. 183, n.

रुक्ष and रूक्ष रू̆क्ष, adj.
 1. Rugged, rough, difficult, Vikr. d. 61 (र्ŭ).
 2. Harsh, unkind, Pañc. iv. d. 62 (रू˚); uncouth, Pañc. v. d. 6 (र्ŭ˚, but cf. Böhtl. Ind. Spr. 805); Bhartṛ. 2, 59 (र्ŭ˚); cruel, Śāk. d. 191 (रू˚).
 3. Austere, Utt. Rāmac. 42, 8 (र्ŭ).
 --Cf. A.S. rug, ruh, ruw; Engl. rough, rugged.
रुक्ष्म रुक्ष्म, Hard, fleshless (?), Rājat. 5, 433 (? perhaps to be changed to रुक्ष).
† रूक्ष् रूक्ष्, i. 10 (rather a denomin. derived from रूक्ष), Par. To be harsh.
